title: Many of Lake Malawi's cichlids live only in that lake
body: UNESCO reports that hundreds of cichlid fish species inhabit Lake Malawi and that nearly all of those in its national park are endemic to the lake. Many are known locally as mbuna.
takeaway: A lake can act like an island for freshwater species when there is no easy route to other waters.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Lake Malawi National Park

title: Tanzania's Ngorongoro Crater is a vast volcanic caldera
body: Ngorongoro Crater lies within a conservation area established in 1959. A caldera is a broad depression made when part of a volcano collapses, leaving a basin surrounded by raised walls.
takeaway: A geological collapse can create a distinctive habitat long after the volcano that shaped it has changed.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ngorongoro Conservation Area

title: A single Sichuan valley rises through several forest ecosystems
body: Jiuzhaigou in northern Sichuan covers about 720 square kilometres and reaches more than 4,800 metres above sea level. Its range of elevations includes several distinct forest ecosystems.
takeaway: Walking uphill can take you through ecological transitions that would otherwise require travelling much farther.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Jiuzhaigou Valley (1992)
